author: WP16
summary: Alpha.1-era chapter on sharp-runtime's parity target and permanent deviations: three outcomes, reflection, GC, delegates, serialization, interop, cryptography, IDisposable and ReaderWriterLockSlim, exception hierarchy, frozen naming, platform limits and __int128. Mostly current at 41b918c9, but serialization narrowed (SerializationInfo value store) and three further permanent deviations exist. The site mentioned the non-goals only in one Tutorial 89 callout; the full treatment is on the parity-and-verification deep dive.

concepts.section: Parity and Permanent Deviations
concepts.text: sharp-runtime targets maximum practical parity (API, semantics, defaults, error messages, algorithms), stronger than name compatibility and narrower than a CLR; deviations are part of the contract.

concepts.section: Three outcomes, not one generic stub
concepts.text: Implementable operations behave like .NET; unrepresentable mechanisms throw NotImplementedException with an explanation; host-missing mechanisms throw PlatformNotSupportedException.

concepts.section: Three outcomes, not one generic stub
concepts.text: The parity/permanent-deviation/platform-limitation taxonomy lets callers and tests tell a design boundary from an environment boundary.

concepts.section: Three outcomes, not one generic stub
concepts.text: A silent success value is not an acceptable fourth category; unsupported operations must still compile.

concepts.section: Three outcomes, not one generic stub
concepts.text: A method whose body is a bare throw NotImplementedException() without justification counts as a stub, not as ported.

concepts.section: Reflection: correctly a stub, not a gap
concepts.text: For Type, Activator and enum reflection a stub is the intended final behaviour, not a placeholder.
tokens: a stub is the intended final behaviour

concepts.section: Reflection: correctly a stub, not a gap
concepts.text: Reflection needs runtime type metadata a compiled C++ binary does not carry; building a type system would be disproportionate to CNA's needs.

concepts.section: Garbage collection: inert compatibility answers, by design
concepts.text: GC.Collect and SuppressFinalize are no-ops; allocation statistics are zero, TryStartNoGCRegion returns false, WaitForFullGCApproach reports NotApplicable, MaxGeneration is 2.

concepts.section: Garbage collection: inert compatibility answers, by design
concepts.text: Callers may keep defensive GC calls so ported code compiles but must not infer heap telemetry from them.

concepts.section: Delegates: a three-tier model, corrected once in the project's own history
concepts.text: The project's delegate description was found inaccurate during an audit on 2026-07-11 and rewritten as three tiers.

concepts.section: Delegates: a three-tier model, corrected once in the project's own history
concepts.text: Tier 1: Action, Func and most *Callback/*EventHandler aliases are std::function: single target, no multicast, no BeginInvoke/EndInvoke.

concepts.section: Delegates: a three-tier model, corrected once in the project's own history
concepts.text: Tier 2: System::Delegate is a real multicast base with Combine, Remove, RemoveAll and GetInvocationList.

concepts.section: Delegates: a three-tier model, corrected once in the project's own history
concepts.text: Tier 3: MulticastAction is built for multicast event fields, removing by token because callables have no target-plus-method equality.

concepts.section: Delegates: a three-tier model, corrected once in the project's own history
concepts.text: EventHandler<TEventArgs> applies the event-field idea to the sender/argument shape and adds an optional replay hook.

concepts.section: Delegates: a three-tier model, corrected once in the project's own history
concepts.text: Only Delegate exposes DynamicInvoke and it always throws NotImplementedException; the alias and event types expose no late-bound call.

concepts.section: Serialization, P/Invoke, and cryptography: three different reasons for the same conclusion
concepts.text: Serialization is out of scope as a scope judgment (not needed for game code), but SerializationInfo is now a real value store for exception signatures.
tokens: scope: not needed for game code

concepts.section: Serialization, P/Invoke, and cryptography: three different reasons for the same conclusion
concepts.text: P/Invoke and interop are out of scope because the project already is native code.

concepts.section: Serialization, P/Invoke, and cryptography: three different reasons for the same conclusion
concepts.text: Encryption, X.509 and SslStream are out of scope by a dated owner decision: correct support needs OpenSSL/mbedTLS or a hand-rolled security-critical implementation.

concepts.section: Serialization, P/Invoke, and cryptography: three different reasons for the same conclusion
concepts.text: The crypto boundary rests on liability and dependency weight, unlike reflection/GC (no meaning) and serialization (scope).

concepts.section: Serialization, P/Invoke, and cryptography: three different reasons for the same conclusion
concepts.text: MD5, SHA, HMAC and PBKDF2 stay in scope; they are not non-cryptographic, HMAC/PBKDF2 inputs are secret, and callers own algorithm choice and review.

concepts.section: IDisposable and the exception hierarchy: parity by pattern, not by mechanism
concepts.text: IDisposable parity targets Dispose()'s contract (idempotent, generally non-throwing), not the using statement; callers choose an explicit call, destructor or scope guard.

concepts.section: IDisposable and the exception hierarchy: parity by pattern, not by mechanism
concepts.text: ReaderWriterLockSlim once ignored millisecondsTimeout, ignored LockRecursionPolicy (deadlock instead of LockRecursionException) and counted readers by membership (nested exit threw, writers starved); all fixed against .NET's TryEnter*LockCore.

concepts.section: IDisposable and the exception hierarchy: parity by pattern, not by mechanism
concepts.text: ReaderWriterLockSlim::Dispose only sets a flag; every entry point checks it first and throws ObjectDisposedException named after the class.
tokens: every entry point checks that flag first

concepts.section: IDisposable and the exception hierarchy: parity by pattern, not by mechanism
concepts.text: About 114 exception classes; 49 derive directly from SystemException, 15 from Exception, the rest via intermediate bases, matching .NET's two-level shape.

concepts.section: IDisposable and the exception hierarchy: parity by pattern, not by mechanism
concepts.text: The root Exception header documents why GetBaseException, ToString, TargetSite and GetObjectData are absent, tracing them to the no-clone, no-reflection and no-serialization decisions.

concepts.section: Naming is a compatibility surface
concepts.text: Properties bind as getXxxProperty()/setXxxProperty(), indexers as getItem()/setItem(); public headers hold 3,080 get...Property( occurrences.

concepts.section: Naming is a compatibility surface
concepts.text: The project's rules freeze broad header renaming because the conventions touch 449+ files and would break CNA.

concepts.section: Naming is a compatibility surface
concepts.text: Porting rules require intcs, nested namespace syntax, and std::ranges instead of LINQ in code the project writes.

concepts.section: Naming is a compatibility surface
concepts.text: System/Linq.hpp exists as a compatibility surface for ported call sites, with zero uses in CNA measured by the project.

concepts.section: Naming is a compatibility surface
concepts.text: The getCurrent -> getCurrentProperty repair (2514bb1f) changed 61 lines in 23 files atomically, keeping no alias.

concepts.section: Two further, narrower accepted boundaries
concepts.text: Platform-limited areas: Sockets and RandomAccess (throw on Emscripten), AppDomain and TimeZoneInfo fallbacks, Process and POSIX signals (POSIX only), NetworkInterface and FileSystemWatcher (Linux only); all compile.

concepts.section: Two further, narrower accepted boundaries
concepts.text: Decimal, Int128 and UInt128 need a native __int128: x86-64 GCC/Clang/MinGW yes, MSVC and i686 MinGW no, a compiler-capability boundary published as SHARP_RUNTIME_HAS_NATIVE_INT128.

concepts.section: Two further, narrower accepted boundaries
concepts.text: The 2026-07-11 decision not to hand-roll 128-bit arithmetic is permanent.

concepts.section: Two further, narrower accepted boundaries
concepts.text: Without native 128-bit support the three headers refuse inclusion, only dependent members disappear, and an i686 regression target guards the boundary.

concepts.section: A documented deviation still needs verification
concepts.text: Permanent gaps still need tests: GC calls stable, Type identity working, DynamicInvoke failing explicitly, unsupported platform calls throwing the promised exception.

concepts.section: A documented deviation still needs verification
concepts.text: At 41b918c9 further permanent deviations are declared: the UTF-8 unit (#2015), no-op Unicode normalization (#2338) and empty tzdata adjustment rules (#2185).
